newsitem.title: USA: IBM sees revs from services for banks - CEO.
newsitem.headline: IBM sees revs from services for banks - CEO.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Louis Gerstner said the computer giant - which just announced an electronic banking venture with 15 banks - will make money from the venture by selling the services of its Global Network and other services.

He also said that the venture, called the Integrion Financial Network, is a for-profit company, but that the companies involved will be making money through the electronic banking services they provide to their customers.
IBM and the banks are developing a range of electronic banking services through the Integrion Financial Network.
Gerstner was not specific on what kind of revenues IBM or any of the companies involved were expecting from the venture.

The companies said they will use the IBM Global Network as the base network for electronic banking, a proprietary network maintained by IBM and used by many corporations as their own network or to conduct commerce with other companies.

The new company, Integrion, will develop an electronic bill payment software system and provide software to connect to the network for the member banks'customers. Consumers will also be able to enter the network via the Internet or any commercial online service, because it will be an open system.
But for now, the group is working on developing a set of open software standards, which the executives said they hope to get out into the industry "very soon."
The companies said the most sensitive banking transactions will run over the IBM Global Network, which they said is more secure than the Internet, but with connections to the Net.
Gerstner said that while the Internet has become a totally new communications medium in the past two years, he said that it is still not yet the "holy grail" companies have hoped for.
"The pay-off is what these institutions do with this," Gerstner told a press conference.
"With this new venture, electronic commerce will take its biggest step to date," Gerstner said. "Integrion is the customer pathway to an array of services...that no bank could provide alone."

He said that he hopes that companies like Intuit Inc, which has its own set of deals with banks for electronic banking software, will develop versions of its popular personal financial software for Integrion.
